newsitem.title: CANADA: FIGURE SKATING-BOURNE AND KRAATZ WIN SKATE CANADA DANCE TITLE.
newsitem.headline: FIGURE SKATING-BOURNE AND KRAATZ WIN SKATE CANADA DANCE TITLE.

text.p: Canadians Shae-Lynn Bourne and Victor Kraatz unveiled their new free dance Sunday and though it's still in the working stage the performance was good enough for first prize at Skate Canada.
"It's only a skeleton compared to what it's going to be," said Bourne, thinking ahead to the world championships in March. "By worlds, all the spices will be added."
World bronze medallists Bourne, 20, and Kraatz, 25, earned $30,000 for their victory in this Champions Series event.
Marina Anissina and Gwendal Peizerat of France took away $18,000 for finishing second ahead of Italy's Barbara Fusar Poli and Maurizio Margaglio, who received $10,000.
Two-time world champion Elvis Stojko of Canada won the men's title and Russian Irina Slutskaya claimed the women's crown Saturday. Germans Mandy Woetzel and Ingo Steuer won the pairs event Friday.
This was the second meet in the six-meet series, with the top skaters qualifying for the series final in Hamilton, Ontario, starting February 28.
The winners' free dance programme had a high-energy start to a selection from High Society Overture. Extracts from Willow Weep for Me and Opus 1 followed.
The Italians were elated to finish third.

Fusar Poli and Margaglio have been together for only two years but were 10th at the 1996 worlds and Sunday they finished ahead of Lithuanians Margarita Drobiazko and Povilas Vanagas, ranked eighth in the world.
"The Lithuanians are very good so for us to finish ahead of them is incredible for us," said Margaglio. "To think of doing this was only a dream."
